## What this is

The **Orbital** template: a scaffold that turns a client's problem statement into a ladder of modules
that runs from nothing to a deliverable, and five working app templates to start from.

**Starting a new project?** Run [`PROTOCOL.md`](../PROTOCOL.md) from S0. Do not read ahead and do not
design anything before the briefing is complete — that is the one rule the whole scaffold rests on.

**Working inside a project already underway?** Read in this order:

1. [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../.decisions/ARCHITECTURE.md) — the conventions and the `AR#` norms
2. [`BRIEFING.md`](../.sources/BRIEFING.md) — the problem everything descends from
3. [`GRAND_PLAN.md`](../.plan/GRAND_PLAN.md) — the ceiling of coherence
4. [`MINIMUM_PLAN.md`](../.plan/MINIMUM_PLAN.md) — the path to the MVP
5. `.plan/LADDER_PLAN_M_<current>.md` — the module in flight
6. [`BUSINESS_RULES.md`](../.decisions/BUSINESS_RULES.md) — the `BR#` norms
7. [`.decisions/`](../.decisions/README.md) — the `ADR-###` register; **never contradict an accepted
   one without writing the one that supersedes it**
8. [`DATA_MODEL.md`](../.sources/DATA_MODEL.md) and [`API_SURFACE.md`](../.sources/API_SURFACE.md) — the
   shapes in play
9. [`TESTS.md`](../.decisions/TESTS.md) and [`DEPENDENCIES.md`](../.decisions/DEPENDENCIES.md) — how it is
   proven and what it needs

[`.team/`](../.team/TEAM.md) is read when the work involves planning, hand-off or deciding who owns a
call.

## The axes

> **The dot in front of the name is deliberate.** It marks a low-level path, read by the harness, not
> by the person who opens the repository to see what the project does. The root keeps the front
> doors; the thinking stays here.

| axis | what it holds |
|---|---|
| [`.sources/`](../.sources/README.md) | the facts a project derives from — briefing, data model, API surface — and the external references that **decided** something |
| [`.decisions/`](../.decisions/README.md) | the `ADR-###` register, and the norms beside it: `ARCHITECTURE` (`AR#`), `BUSINESS_RULES` (`BR#`), `TESTS`, `DEPENDENCIES` |
| [`.plan/`](../.plan/README.md) | what comes next and what was put off; the ladder machinery a project fills; the template's [roadmap](../.plan/ROADMAP.md) |
| [`.orders/`](../.orders/README.md) | the Orders — the contract that dispatches the work, immutable and numbered, one open at a time |
| [`.constraints/`](../.constraints/README.md) | what the project **forbids itself** — read before proposing |
| [`.changelog/`](../.changelog/README.md) | how the version number moves; the record is the root `CHANGELOG.md` |
| [`.team/`](../.team/TEAM.md) | the roles — PO, DV, QA, DA — and how agents run over the ladder ([`ORCHESTRATION.md`](../.team/ORCHESTRATION.md)) |
| `.shortcuts/` | this file, and [`.virtual/`](.virtual/README.md) — the agent's first peek: what is ongoing, what is only backlog |

The four in the middle are a cycle, and that is the order to read them in:
**decide → schedule → commission → record.** [`PROTOCOL.md`](../PROTOCOL.md) sits at the root of the
set: it is the algorithm that fills all of it.

[`.history/`](../.history/README.md) sits beside them and **is not an axis**: it is the attic, where a
superseded document leaves the reading path without leaving the repository.

`Docs/.guidelines/` is the only guideline set (`ADR-002`). Client material lives in `.scope/` and is
never published (`ADR-003`).

## The template's map, in five lines

1. Projects are `<CONCEPT>_<DOMAIN>` inside `<APP>_ORBITAL`, five domains, and the arrow points inward
   only: `_PANEL → _DRIVE → _CORE → _ENGINE`, with `_PROBE` outside (`AR1`–`AR8`).
2. A project's source of truth is its briefing; the grand plan, the backlog, the minimum plan and the
   ladder derive from it, in that order (`PROTOCOL` S0–S9).
3. A plan never states a business rule: rules live in `BUSINESS_RULES.md`, and a plan only quotes them.
4. A gap is a question, never a guess: an unknown briefing field is `[TBD — owner]`, and nothing is
   derived over it.
5. Every task cites a norm and names its test, and execution opens only through a gate
   ([`PLANNING.md`](../.plan/PLANNING.md#gate-formula)).

## The id grammar

| prefix | means | lives in |
|---|---|---|
| `ADR-###` | decision — architecture, limits, duties | [`.decisions/README.md`](../.decisions/README.md) |
| `AR<n>` | architecture rule | [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../.decisions/ARCHITECTURE.md) |
| `BR<n>` | business rule | [`BUSINESS_RULES.md`](../.decisions/BUSINESS_RULES.md) |
| `D1`–`D3` | difficulty — Simple, Dense, Very dense | a scale, not a register |
| `B<n>` | backlog item | [`BACKLOG.md`](../.plan/BACKLOG.md) |
| `M<n>` | module — one step of the ladder | `.plan/LADDER_PLAN_M_<n>.md` |
| `F0`–`F6` | phase — fixed, in every module | inside a module |
| `T<nn>` | task — one commit | inside a phase |
| `ORD-####` | Order | [`.orders/`](../.orders/README.md) |

A **norm** is any `ADR-###`, `AR<n>` or `BR<n>`, and every task cites one. A fully qualified task
looks like **`M2.F3.T04`** and appears in the checklist, the trace and the commit subject. `ADR-008`
replaces this grammar with `M##.D##.T##`; the ladder documents move to it in roadmap module 2.

Normative force in prose uses **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, **MAY**, **NOTE**. The bold keyword
is the norm; the same word in ordinary prose is not.

## Commands

```bash
dotnet build _ORBITAL.slnx
```

```bash
dotnet sln _ORBITAL.slnx list
```

Tests run **project by project**, never through the solution, so that a project with a pre-build step
cannot drag an unrelated toolchain into the test run:

```bash
dotnet test <APP>_ORBITAL/<CONCEPT>_PROBE
```

Adding a project — only after the confirmation `AR9` requires, as a task of the module that needs it:

```bash
dotnet new classlib -o <APP>_ORBITAL/<CONCEPT>_<DOMAIN>
```

```bash
dotnet sln _ORBITAL.slnx add <APP>_ORBITAL/<CONCEPT>_<DOMAIN>
```

## Agent working files

The root [`CLAUDE.md`](../../../CLAUDE.md) is published and only points here (`ADR-011`). A root
`AGENTS.md` stays local and gitignored: it is personal working setup, not published content.

## The project's vocabulary

The terms coined here — norm, invariant, gate, phase, module, the domains — are defined once, in
[`ARCHITECTURE.md`](../.decisions/ARCHITECTURE.md) §7.
